tagline: Two roads up one valley, a canal between them.
intro: Out of Kingston, where the old King's Highway crossed the Millstone River, the byway splits in two and runs north up a long, narrow valley. River Road winds beside the Millstone on the west. Canal Road follows the Delaware and Raritan Canal on the east, and the land between them is state park, towpath and all. The loop runs about 25 miles, with Millstone and East Millstone at its north end.

For a century the canal carried coal, farm goods and manufactured goods toward New York. The roads are older. They began as Lenape trails along and across the river, and the Continental Army marched up this valley in 1777 after the victory at Princeton.

moments.title: Rocky Hill
moments.text: Before the roads were improved, wagon traffic knew this rocky ground as the Devil's Featherbed. Washington camped here at Rockingham, the Berrien family's house, in 1783.

moments.title: Griggstown
moments.text: The visitor center keeps an 1850s kitchen in a canal bridgetender's house. For three decades neighbors reported a ghostly cow along the canal. In 2002 a feral bull turned up in a ditch.

moments.title: Millstone
moments.text: The county seat until the British burned it in 1779. It is named for the river, which took its own name from a millstone somebody dropped in it.

practical: The byway visitor center at 2 Griggstown Causeway is open weekend afternoons, 1 to 4, from April through October. The byway's sponsor points travelers to National Weather Service flood levels at the bridges along the route.
